stem:
A Massachusetts retail pharmacy reviews nonsterile preparations. It is not relying on a special shortage enforcement policy or a veterinary office-use exception. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A pharmacy distinguishes simple reconstitution exactly under the manufacturer’s approved instructions from compounding.
A prescriber documents a patient-specific medical need for a significant difference from an available commercial product.
A pharmacist adding flavoring to a requested Schedule VI medication evaluates and records concentration and stability effects.
A pharmacy treats crushing hazardous tablets into a suspension as ordinary nonhazardous tablet counting.
A pharmacy dispensing a patient-specific compound links the preparation to the required valid patient prescription.

stem:
A Massachusetts sterile pharmacy evaluates a preparation and its release conditions. No unmentioned USP exception or Board waiver is being used. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A facility assigns a longer-category BUD without the corresponding facility and testing conditions because the solution appears clear.
A pharmacist treats a passing filter-integrity result as proof that endotoxin is absent.
A pharmacist assumes meeting the preparation’s release date alone establishes stability throughout a prolonged implanted infusion.
A pharmacist distinguishes a source vial’s puncture/in-use limit from the finished CSP’s assigned BUD.
A facility accepts an unrelated CE certificate in place of the required hands-on aseptic competency assessment.

stem:
A pharmacist evaluates handling and sourcing controls. Hazardous-drug exposure, controlled-substance scheduling, and FDA outsourcing registration are distinct classifications. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A pharmacy exempts a listed hazardous drug from exposure controls because it is not federally scheduled.
A facility reassesses exposure controls when an intact hazardous tablet will instead be crushed for compounding.
A pharmacy checks Massachusetts authority as well as federal outsourcing registration before sourcing for MA patients.
A purchaser recognizes that FDA outsourcing registration is not FDA approval of every compounded product.
A facility distinguishes deactivation, decontamination, cleaning, and disinfection when designing the cleaning process.

stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacy is responding to a quality event. Patient protection, internal CQI, product recall, and agency reporting are evaluated separately. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A pharmacy keeps CQI records and separately completes any applicable external serious-event report.
A pharmacy restarts an agency reporting clock when the MOR eventually reads an event already known to pharmacy personnel.
A pharmacy evaluates related batches sharing the implicated component lot or process when a test fails.
A pharmacy records affected preparations and maintains the required defective-preparation log and related disposition records.
A pharmacy promptly recalls and quarantines a preparation it knows or has reason to believe is defective.
